learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of the essential grammatical and morphosyntactic structures of the English language at B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

The student will be able to apply the acquired text analysis knowledge to autonomously read and understand texts on the topics covered. This ability applies to receptive skills (reading and listening).
The student will be able to interpret and synthesize B1 level texts in English in a personal and effective way.
The student will be able to communicate and argue simply about events, topics, and projects related to their own experience or facts, explaining their opinion.
The student must have developed the learning abilities necessary to undertake autonomous study of linguistic knowledge that goes beyond textbook learning.

syllabus_topics: Grammar: Simple and progressive verb tenses in active and passive voice (present, past, future)
Grammar: Modal verbs (can, may, might, should etc)
Grammar: Verbs that take the infinitive and verbs that take the gerund
Grammar: Verb patterns and word patterns
Specialized language: relevant to the course of study
teaching_methods: Online presentations and exercises on the CLA platform

assessment_methods.method: Written test: reading comprehension with true/false or multiple-choice questions
Written test: lexical and grammatical exercises
Written test: multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank exercises

assessment_rules: The written test consists of 50 to 70 questions and is passed with 75% correct answers. The grade is not indicated, only a 'SUITABLE' (minimum 75% correct answers) or 'NOT SUITABLE' (below 75% correct answers). The written test verifies the achievement of the competencies indicated in the learning outcomes.
bibliography: Material available on the CLA platform (PowerPoint, PDF readings, grammatical and lexical exercises, writing and listening activities)
